## Overview

```{r echo=FALSE, out.width="50%", out.extra='style="float:right; padding:10px"'}
knitr::include_graphics("images/CCDI_Hub.png") 
```
This is an adaptation of the [VCF Table Viewer](https://github.com/CBIIT-CGBB/VCF_Table_Viewer) shiny app that is tailored to access Variant Call Format (VCF) files from the [Childhood Cancer Data Initiative (CCDI) Hub](https://ccdi.cancer.gov/explore?tab=3) on the [Cancer Genomics Cloud](https://www.cancergenomicscloud.org) (CGC) platform.  The purpose is to enable easy examination of annotated variants by extracting them from the difficult-to-read VCF format and displaying them in an easy-to-navigate table format.  If the corresponding BAM file is available, you can also visualize the read pileups at the location of a called variant. The assumption is that you are viewing a filtered set of variants (under 10,000) for manual inspection - the app is not designed to load full VCF files from whole-genome shotgun sequencing experiments, for example.  

## Input
The default input is a manifest file derived from the CCDI Hub.  The script for generating the manifest file is available on [Github](https://github.com/msierk/VCF_Table_Viewer_CCDI).  This manifest file has all of the VCF files from all the studies available on the CCDI Hub, with matching BAM and/or CRAM alignment files.  

**It is essential that the VCF files that you want to view have been copied to your project-files directory on CGC.**  *Note: The VCF Table Viewer is only designed to read in 10,000 variants, so it gives a warning if your selected VCF file is too large.*  If you wish to view the BAM or CRAM file, the associated tabix-indexed file (.bam.bai or .cram.crai) must be present in the same directory.  Some CCDI BAM files have existing index files and some do not - if the index file does not exist you will need to generate it. If a sample has both BAM and CRAM files the BAM file is loaded.

To copy the files you want to view to CGC you follow these steps:  

1. Go to the CCDI Hub and use the filtering tools to identify the files you wish to view.  
2. Add the files to your Cart.  
3. Select "Copy to CGC".  
4. Select the destination project in CGC. (Must be set up first.)  
5. The files will be copied to the project-files folder within a few minutes.  

If you provide your own manifest file in .csv format, it must contain the following columns: VCFFileName, ParticipantID, SampleID. Optional columns include StudyID, VCFFileSize, caller, BAMFileName, and CRAMFileName.

You select a StudyID, which then populates the ParticipantID selection menu.  Once you select a Participant, the SampleID menu is populated.  You can optionally filter based upon FileAccess (Open or Controlled (the default is both are shown)) and caller (default is consensus). The list of available callers is below. You can use ‘unknown’ if the caller is unknown or is not in the list, but the app may not parse the VCF file properly.

Available variant callers:

* haplotypecaller 
* deepvariant 
* mutect2 
* strelka2 
* lancet 
* manta 
* svaba 
* vardict 
* unknown 

You can also enter in a file with columns of gene symbols that you want highlighted in the table.  Select the columns you want highlighted.

## Output
### Table
Once you hit "Load Table" the selected VCF is converted into a table.  The columns are sortable and searchable. Only a subset of columns are shown - you can select from the dropdown menu to view other columns, or hide ones you don't want to see. If you select rows they stay highlighted and can be used for the BAM viewer or Plot.  You can also download the selected rows to an Excel file.   

### Filtering Options
#### Mutations
The default is to filter for Significant Mutations. You can add Less Significant Mutations, or select 'None' for no filtering.

[Significant Mutations]{.underline}

* missense_variant
* stop_gained
* splice_donor_variant
* splice_acceptor_variant
* splice_region_variant
* frameshift_variant
* disruptive_inframe_insertion
* disruptive_inframe_deletion
* conservative_inframe_deletion
* conservative_inframe_insertion
* start_lost
* stop_lost

[Less Significant Mutations]{.underline}

* stop_retained_variant
* 5_prime_UTR_premature_start_codon_gain_variant
* 5_prime_UTR_variant
* 3_prime_UTR_variant
* synonymous_variant

#### Population Allele Frequencies
You can enter in a value for the maximum allele frequency to include from the GnomAD database.

### Input Manifest
The manifest used to populate the selection menus is shown in the Input Manifest tab.  You can search here for particular subjects or files if you aren't sure which ones to pick in the menus.

### BAM Viewer
For the BAM Viewer to work, you must have the BAM file that the VCF calls were made from in the input manifest file in the project files directory, along with the associated tabix index file. The variant positions from the rows selected in the table are in the dropdown menu - selecting one will load all the samples for that patient into the IGV viewer.  Click "Remove Tracks" to clear loaded tracks.

### Plots
A plot of the allele frequencies for the variants selected in the table is created.  This is most useful when there are multiple samples present in the VCF and you want to see the change over the different samples.
